summary: Configure near-real-time SIEM delta push with dynamic rule-based field redaction and signed resume tokens for monthly compliance portal
description:
Issue summary:
Helios requests a near-real-time SIEM push that delivers incremental (delta) audit events to their Splunk Cloud instance. Key requirements are: (1) dynamic rule-based field redaction controlled by a customer-specified policy DSL, (2) deterministic ordering and signed resume tokens so their compliance portal can resume ingestion from a precise checkpoint, and (3) chunk-level HMACs and delivery receipts for tamper-evident monthly audit packages.

Impact:
Helios will use Redwood exports as their primary source-of-truth for regulatory reporting. Without the requested guarantees they cannot close monthly evidence windows for several funds, which delays audits and could trigger contractual penalties. They are on an enterprise contract and expect production-grade SLAs.

Environment:
Production tenant: tenant-hel-001, region us-east-1, export target Splunk Cloud HEC via mTLS endpoint at https://ingest.helios.splunkcloud.com:8088. Current export configured as batched S3 snapshots; Helios needs a continuous push option with delta/resume semantics.

Requested deliverables:
- A production-ready webhook/export profile that pushes delta batches to Helios with deterministic sequence IDs and signed resume tokens (one-time-resume-tokens / ORTs) per chunk.
- Support for a lightweight policy DSL provided by Helios to redact fields based on name, JSON path, and regex rules at delivery time (policy applied server-side prior to signing).
- Chunk-level HMAC signed with rotating KEK and proof manifest delivered daily to the customer S3 for reconciliation.
- A short runbook (1 page) describing how to rotate KEKs, how ORTs behave on resume after partial failures, and how customers can verify chunk integrity locally.

Acceptance criteria:
- Helios can start a stream and receive progressive delta payloads with ordered sequence IDs and ORTs.
- When a resume token is submitted, Redwood returns only the next chunk(s) deterministically; no duplicates or gaps for a given stream snapshot window.
- Redaction policy is applied and evidenced in the manifest (field-level redaction markers, not original values).
- Daily manifest contains chunk IDs, HMACs, timestamp window, and proof-of-KEK-version used.

Additional notes from customer:
They are particularly concerned about 'redaction drift' (policy changes that retrospectively affect previously delivered events). Their ask: policies are applied at delivery time only; manifest should include policy version used for each chunk so auditors can trace decisions.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer provides Splunk HEC endpoint and mTLS certs
Enable experimental 'delta-push' export profile for tenant-hel-001 via Console (feature flag: export.delta_push=true)
Start a small stream scoped to 1 hour of events and request 'policyVersion=v1.0' in export configuration
Observe that chunks are posted to Helios and ORTs are returned in the X-Resume-Token header
Intentionally interrupt the network after chunk 3 and resume using the last ORT to confirm deterministic continuation

comments: 2026-03-14T09:02 - Helios (securityops@helios-am.com): We need per-chunk policy versioning in the manifest. Retroactive policy changes must not invalidate existing manifests.
2026-03-14T10:15 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. We'll propose a manifest schema that includes 'policyVersion' and 'keKVersion'. Attaching draft below.

2026-03-14T11:45 - Engineering (Liam): Spun up experimental delta stream in staging. Observed deterministic ordering but ORTs expire after 30s by default; will propose configurable TTL and one-time use semantics.
2026-03-15T07:30 - Support (Aisha): Provided Helios a temporary staging endpoint and instructions to validate chunk HMACs and ORT resume behavior. Waiting for customer validation.

2026-03-15T12:05 - Helios: Validation done on staging. Found that regex-based rule '/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/' removed date tokens but left partial context; requesting 'replace-with=MASK(<field_name>)' option in DSL.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Current export pipeline signs entire chunk payload after redaction; if policy applied inconsistently across pipeline stages (console vs service) it could create mismatches between delivered payload and manifest hmac.

Finding: Console stored policyVersion as a string but export-service parsed policy JSON and dropped whitespace leading to canonicalization differences. Need canonical policy serialization before signing.
Telemetry: dashboard link - https://grafana.redwood.example.org/d/exports/delta-streams?orgId=1&var-tenant=tenant-hel-001 shows chunk-retries spike at 08:13 and ORT generation events.
Plan: implement canonical JSON serializer for policy DSL, add policyVersion to chunk manifest, and expose ORT TTL as configuration per export profile.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: switched Helios to staging delta endpoint; we applied canonical policy serializer and increased ORT TTL to 10 minutes for testing. Next actions: (1) engineering to merge KEK rotation and manifest schema PR, (2) support to coordinate production cutover with Helios on 2026-03-20, (3) create a customer-facing one-page runbook on resume semantics and KEK rotation.
